On May 9, 2023, it was released as an official add-on for the Doom Classic Unity port.

425889.overview: A MS-DOS Fighting Game featuring two combatants named Sukido (Policeman) and  Urotso (Street Man).  Wielding energy weapons, they compete in a tournament style battle to be the best there is.

449143.overview:
Bonus is an Israeli computerized version of the word game Scrabble, completely in Hebrew. The game can be played between two players or against the computer.

The name of the game is derived from the bonus squares placed outside of the regular game table. Successfully placing a letter on one of these squares may earn the player a bonus, automatically or through the completion of a mini-game.

449624.overview:
"Bird Brain," developed by the staff of Emerald Valley Publishing, was published as part of their "Home Computer Magazine." In this game, you control a hungry tropical bird searching for food while taking a break from brooding on her eggs. The objective is to catch a fish swimming in the river below. The bird's movement is controlled by flapping its wings, similar to the game mechanics in "Joust," with additional momentum control to the right or left. Precise movements are crucial, as missteps can lead to the bird falling into the water or being swept away by waves.

After catching a fish, it must be returned to the nest within a set time limit, or the bird will die. Performance is timed, and faster completions result in higher scores. The game's difficulty increases by speeding up the action and making the bird harder to control.

449625.overview:
"Bowling Champ!!" is a straightforward bowling game for one to four players featuring text-based graphics. Players start by entering the number of participants, their names, and selecting a difficulty level. The gameplay proceeds from left to right on the screen. The ball oscillates at the left end of the lane, and pressing the space bar releases it, sending it toward the pins on the right. Scoring follows the standard rules of bowling.

Upon exiting the game, players are shown an advertisement for "The Techstaff Amazing Preview Disk," a menu-driven catalog of IBM shareware and public domain programs by the publisher.

449628.overview:
Daredevil Biker Dave is out to wow the crowd - he's brought his two-wheeled speed demon for a streak of daring car jumps. After each successful leap, the ramps are moved farther apart, and another car is added.  There's also a hoop jump halfway through the course, although the Atari version offers a "rookie" mode without the hoop.  The ultimate goal is to jump nine cars at a time, and Biker Dave has five bikes primed and ready.  But there's one little thing Biker Dave overlooked... none of them have any brakes.

The only control is acceleration: to pull off his fearless acrobatics, Dave will need precise control of the throttle and an eye on the speed meter.  Go too slow or too fast at the wrong time, and he'll receive a painful crash course in gravity and friction.

453715.overview:
Bannercatch is an educational action game for two players. The game is a variation of capture the flag; two human players compete against Max and his team of robots. To win the game, the players need to work as a team to travel to Max's zone of the playfield, capture the flag, and bring it back safely back before Max is able to capture the player's flag. Each time the players successfully capture one of Max's flags, part of his face will be revealed; the goal is to try to see all of Max's face.

To help with this quest, the game includes maps which provide an overview of the entire playing field (each player will only be able to see a small portion of the screen at a time). Also, hints about his flag's whereabouts can be gained by tricking Max into telling about it. This is done by positioning a player over one of the robot sensors and attempting to communicate with Max disguised as one of his robots. Since Max talks to his robots in binary, the player will need to translate a series of binary numbers to convince Max to reveal clues about his flags' location. At any time during the game, the player can freeze the action; this allows for checking the maps or taking a rest.

The game features five different levels of difficulty along with a demonstration mode. Points are earned for successfully capturing the flag, tagging a robot which is carrying your flag, and winning the game.

454072.overview: Blueberry is an adventure game, developed and published by Coktel Vision

454387.overview: You belong to the C.R.B. (Ball Breaking Corps), a team founded with a single objective: to destroy all the G.H.F.E. (Spherical Stinking Gases) that have invaded the Earth, coming from the Orion Nebula. To do this, you must move from city to city, starting with Seville, making use of the multiple weapons that have been put at your disposal. There is no time to lose, the world is in your hands.

454401.overview:
An adventure in anatomy.

Do you know...
Where the coccyx is located?
Why the flexor pollicis brevis muscle is important?
When are twins formed?

You'll find the answers to these questions and many more when you explore the new multimedia interactive Bodyworks 3.0- An Adventure in Anatomy.

455097.overview: B.A.D. is a fixed-screen shooter where players must repel attacks from the Martian commander Rupert. The ship is confined to the lower part of the screen and can only move left and right. The objective is to eliminate all enemy waves to complete each level. Defeated enemies may drop credits or power-ups that enhance the ship’s defensive and offensive capabilities. While most power-ups are beneficial, one can completely disarm the ship. Upgrades can also be purchased in the in-game shop using collected credits, accessible at any time without pausing the action. The game features eight levels and a high-score list.

455184.overview:
Bump & Bomp is a kind and very nice puzzle game, created, as the developers themselves write, under the impression of the imperishable Soko-Ban and its clone Kurtan. You won't find many mentions of this game, but the most interesting thing is that it was created by the Ukrainian (!) team by order of one of the German companies.

In a nutshell, I explain the rules, if the above names mean nothing to you: the main character wanders around the level (it is a system of rooms and corridors, more like a labyrinth), who needs to move all the boxes in the corridors to the marked places (in general, to put things in order). At the same time, the box cannot be lifted or pulled towards you - only pushed forward. The ornate design of the corridors does not contribute to a successful and painless passage at all - the box is easy to drive into a corner or into such a "nook" from where it is simply impossible to get it! The minimum number of moves and time spent give the maximum number of points.

456132.overview: The Berenstain Bears: Volume Two - Learning at Home or want to try this educational video game, Published in 1993 by Compton's New Media, The Berenstain Bears: Volume Two - Learning at Home was an above-average licensed title title in its time.

456478.overview:
!Bingo Granny! is a text-based game without graphics. All interactions with the game (except for "n" for no and "y" for yes) are multiple-choice.

The player controls an old woman of 99 years (and 0 days) and the goal is to stay alive until 100. There are a number of necessary aspects to consider: eating, using the toilet, sleeping and entertainment. The two important resources are pills (energy pills, crack pills, butt plug pills and happy pills) and money (used to buy pills and food). Besides receiving 25 dollars from the welfare office each day, the main source of income is playing bingo. Except for pressing enter to advance to the next number, the bingo process is automatic.

456621.overview: Bagasaurus is a game in which children control a dinosaur. The player has to move the Bagasaurus to the correct answer to questions/tasks which are presented at the bottom of the screen. One example is to pick up an animal which has a tail, picking up a dog would be a correct answer. In response to a correct answer the Bagasaurus will do a little jig. In addition to this there is also a story telling mode.

457468.overview:
Big Bird's Special Delivery is a preschool computer game where the player can practice classification of objects. In a playful setting of shops, Big Bird and Little Bird work to delivery mail to one of four locations. This computer activity aims to teach children understanding of form class and function. The objects are controlled by pressing one of three keys on the computer keyboard to control Little Bird.

When a round of play is completed the shops will light up after the mail is correctly delivered. If there is a mail mix-up, the shopkeepers gently point out mistakes and encourage the child to try again.

457480.overview:
THE BERENSTAIN BEARS - LEARN ABOUT COUNTING is an educational game for children aged 4-7. It was published by Softprime Inc. in 1991. The game was developed by Britannica Software and runs on the DOS platform.

The game features the popular children's book characters, The Berenstain Bears, and was developed to teach preschool and elementary-grade kids about basic counting. The game progresses by counting the different objects shown on the screen. There are six different setups in the game, and the player can choose to play any of them. The setups range from counting objects of different geometrical figures on the screen, to counting objects in a graphical representation, to basic addition and subtraction.

For every correct answer, the Bear does a happy dance, while every wrong answer gets a sad face from the Bear. Every question needs to be answered correctly before moving on to the next question. The player can enter the correct answer through the keyboard. Arrow keys are used to move the Bear, A key to move back into the main menu, and Enter key to select.

457993.overview:
Boleivol Beach (1991/1992) is a rare, obscure sports release from Ediciones Manali. In typical fashion for the publisher's budget catalog, the title misspelled the Spanish word for volleyball ("Voleibol").

The Gameplay Mechanics: The game simplifies beach volleyball into a flat, 2D side-scrolling profile perspective. It centers entirely on a 1-on-1 matchup (one man vs. one man) rather than the standard olympic 2-on-2 beach rules. Players use basic direction keys to shuffle across the sand, timing a single action button to jump, block, or spike the ball over the net.

The Multiplayer Option: It features a local co-op "hot-seat" versus option, allowing two players to compete against each other simultaneously on a single shared keyboard.

The Technical Style: True to Manali's low-budget software architecture, the file sizes are minimal. It renders the sunny beach stadium using large, blocky, 4-color style sprites with simple internal PC-speaker beeps.

458007.overview:
Bios is a horizontally-scrolling shooter in which players face the challenge of protecting humanity from an alien threat. The objective is to escort scientists to safety while navigating dangerous terrain. The player pilots a spacecraft capable of moving in all directions and shooting forward, striving to reach the end of the single level and defeat the final boss.

Throughout the journey, players must shoot or evade various hazards, including aliens, asteroids, and other obstacles. Two power-ups can be collected during gameplay: additional fuel to extend flight time, and a weapon upgrade that enables a triple shot. Running out of fuel or sustaining excessive damage results in a game over.

458010.overview:
Brocha Gorda is an arcade game in which the player takes the role of a painter whose job is to cover each stage with paint while avoiding roaming enemies. Successfully painting enough of the playfield allows the painter to move on to the next stage.

Brocha Gorda is played from a top-down perspective across a series of single-screen levels. The player moves the painter around the playfield, leaving a trail of paint behind to gradually cover the stage. Enemies patrol the area and must be avoided while painting the remaining sections.

Each completed stage leads to a new screen with a fresh layout and increasingly challenging enemy patterns, requiring more careful planning and movement to paint the required area without being caught.

458012.overview:
In a dystopian future, the Bionic Police are the last remaining force capable of maintaining order. Players assume the role of a Bionic Police Officer tasked with rescuing the wife of Don Tequito, the wealthiest tycoon in the city, who has been kidnapped by a street gang.

The player character moves forward but cannot move backward. They can adjust the angle of their gun to fire horizontally or vertically upwards to combat various enemies. Occasionally, a mutated enemy approaches from behind, prompting the character to look backward to scare it off—however, shooting or moving is not possible in this position.

The game consists of five levels where players must fend off combinations of five enemy types while progressing to the level's exit. The final stage culminates in a boss fight against the gang leader.

458455.overview:
In Blackjack, the first player to get their cards closest to 21 without going over wins.

The value of each card is determined by its number. The "K," "Q," and "J" count as 10, while the "Ace," in its "wild" role, can be valued at 1 or 11 depending on whether the player is going over 21 or not.

458984.overview: The Brick is an Arkanoid clone embodied in the interior of a mechanic system. As such, you will have to help the racket (in this case, a nut), to impulse the ball in order to break as much bricks as possible, although there would be others that will be indestructible by your hit. To make your work more complex, there will be some flying enemies that will modify the trajectory of your ball and in the worst of the cases even shot at you, thus reducing your energy bar. In order to avoid being defeated by these creatures, you have one laser which just one projectile that recharges itself occasionally, so you will have to use it wisely too.

459116.overview: Bolera is a bowling game featuring a one-click control system. An arrow moves rapidly up and down the screen, and when the player presses a key, its movement gradually slows until it comes to a stop. The bowling ball is then automatically launched in the direction indicated by the arrow's final position. Up to four players can compete against each other.

459480.overview:
Best Drive is a top-down action game where players control a car with the objective of reaching the end of each level within a set time limit. Players can accelerate and steer left or right to navigate the course. The game features two types of alternating levels: street level (players must avoid collisions with other vehicles) and desert levels (players navigate around environmental obstacles such as rocks and oil puddles). After completing the fourth level, the game cycles back to the first and continues in a loop.

A session ends if the player collides with too many obstacles or fails to meet the time limit. The score increases continuously as the car progresses, and the primary goal is to finish the game with a high enough score to achieve the leaderboard's top position.

459483.overview:
Bolix was ACA Softs first game they developed.

Do not expect anything especially exciting. The graphics remind me of a lot of amateur games and I have not managed to make it work with sound (does anyone have a version in which it works?).

The game consists of building the roads properly so that a ball that comes out of the top of the screen arrives safely to the bottom of it.

459485.overview: Bicis is a Spanish side-scrolling bicycle racing game. The gameplay is defined by a "button-mashing" mechanic, where the cyclist’s speed increases in proportion to the frequency of the player's key presses.

465539.overview:
The game is turn-based: each turn represents one month of market activities, and allows you to eyeball the market trends, get the lowdown on various properties, buy/sell them, trade in options and and take out loans. You start out with $35,000 in cash and the status of Novice, which carries some limitations like lower loans and high closing costs on sales. As you increase your net worth, becoming an Investor or a Banker, the limitations relax and you gain better leverage.

The goal is to achieve the status of Baron by piling up a net worth of $1,000,000 within 60 months, but if you pull that off, you may still opt to go for the next million and see how quick you can get there. On the other hand, a lack of business savvy may leave you bankrupt. Up to 14 players may record their status and history, although only one can play at a time. A single game session may be saved to disk and resumed later.

465541.overview:
Battle Tank: Kursk to Berlin is a computer wargame for multiple systems, covering the events of the Soviet victory over Nazi Germany in World War II, starting from the Battle of Kursk in July 1943 to the fall of Berlin in May 1945.

Players can control the German and/or the Soviet sides, or the computer can take on one or both roles. The game is text-only, and came with a board and physical pieces to allow the player to keep track of the location of theirs and enemy units. There are a total of eight scenarios to choose from, and the player can also create custom scenarios. The player takes on the role of scenario commander, and issues orders to different units. Groupings may or may not follow commands, and messages and reporting may become skewed to represent fog of war.

465542.overview: The Berenstain Bears: Treehouse Classroom combines the content of The Berenstain Bears: Volume One - Learning at Home and Volume Two. It adds a new intro video with a song and the option to switch between upstairs (Volume One) and downstairs (Volume Two).

465543.overview:
From time before human memory, great automated war machines were created by an unknown alien race. These Berserkers, programmed to eliminate all life that they encounter, still roam the galaxy.

Gameplay occurs in a 10 system star cluster. Each player has a home base and can send out merchant ships to establish production bases in other systems. The player's goal is to strengthen defenses and construct a fleet of their own vessels to counter the Berserker threat. The player can create customized ships or choose from predefined vessels that will take a varying number of resources to produce. The player can possess a maximum fleet of 10 vessels. Each base has a technology and productivity statistic. Technology defines how advanced of ship a base can build, while productivity determines how fast it can build. Each base also has a defensive rating to determine their strength against Berserker attack.

465545.overview:
Bouncy Bee Learns Words is an educational game designed to help children ages 5 - 10 learn word recognition and improve reading skills through several activities and games featuring an animated bee:

Shopping for Words: This activity uses a store window to display pictures and words. The activity is designed to help children read and pronounce different words and also includes an option to help typing and spelling.

Grandfather's Beehive: This activity is designed to help children practice left to right eye movement by using moving words on the screen. A target word is provided, and children need to press the spacebar when they see a matching word.

Filling the Honeycomb: Filling the Honeycomb is a word matching, hand-eye coordination game. The goal of the game is to fill in empty spaces in a honeycomb by matching words to a target word. Various words appear in the empty spaces and the space can only be filled in when the correct word flashes in the space; as the game progresses the honeycomb becomes larger and has more empty spaces to fill.

Antagram Word Game: Antagrams is a word recognition game. At the start of each round, marching ants are scattered randomly in a field; when the game begins they slowly move into formation spelling a word. The faster children can recognize the word before it's fully completed, the more points are earned.

465547.overview: Brány Skeldalu is a Czech dungeon crawler. The player controls a group of adventurers - at the beginning one has to create three characters. The gender of the character is determined by clicking on the appropriate portrait (player can choose from seven portraits and this choice also determines the paper-doll that one sees in the inventory); the game then offers the choice of one of the four available classes: Fighter, Wizard, Thief or Ranger. Moving the dot from the center of the octogram, in which diagonal angles are the four main classes, player can create any possible combination of each adjacent classes - for example, it is possible to create pure Wizard or Wizard-Ranger hybrid, but not the Wizard-Fighter hybrid. The position of the dot on the creation chart then determines the number of points one can distribute between the statistics of the character. There are only four base statistics, namely Strength, Magic Use, Agility and Dexterity. The secondary statistics like weapon proficiencies, experience or defenses can change during the gameplay.

465548.overview: Bridge Champion with Omar Sharif is an implementation of the classic card game bridge. Play against the computer or other players via hot seat or local network. All rules are included and an extensive tutorial helps you to get into the game. Also included are commentaries and tips by bridge champion Omar Sharif.

465550.overview:
Backgammon is a 1-player versus computer backgammon game for DOS.

The player competes against computer opponent Max. There are five levels of opponent difficulty. All rolls and moves are graphically displayed on the screen. Pieces are moved by typing move coordinates. The player can set up custom boards, ask the computer for move advice, display scores, or allow doubling.

465551.overview:
Championship Blackjack is a conversion of the ubiquitous casino game, challenging up to six human players to rack up money by beating the dealer's hand. You can fine-tune the precise variant of Blackjack you wish to play: the game comes with five predefined rule sets, and each rule can be further tweaked individually.

One of the two game modes is "Fun Blackjack" - initial bankrolls are set by the players, and any number of hands may be played. The built-in hint system can provide advice according to two different strategies (basic or point-count). The other mode is Tournament: all players start with $500, the number of hands is set in advance, and hints are disabled.

466003.overview: Barbie PC Fashion Design & Color places the player in the role of a fashion designer working with Barbie-themed outfits using a selection of tools and color palettes. Players choose clothing items and apply colors and patterns to customize their appearance.

466023.overview:
Barney Bear Goes to the Farm is an educational children’s game in which the anthropomorphic protagonist Barney Bear visits his grandparents’ farm. Throughout the game, players explore various farm environments and engage in simple, age-appropriate activities designed to teach basic skills and concepts consistent with preschool learning themes.

Players guide Barney through a series of interactive, picture-book style screens that combine simple puzzles and exploratory elements suitable for young children. Interaction is primarily point-and-click using the keyboard or mouse. Activities incorporate visual and auditory feedback to reinforce events on the farm and support early learning.

466091.overview:
Battle Fire is a top-down arcade shooter set during World War I. The game places the player in the role of a military pilot engaged in aerial combat against enemy aircraft, with the action unfolding across a series of scrolling battlefields representing air engagements of the period.

The player controls an aircraft viewed from a top-down perspective in vertically scrolling stages. Enemy planes enter the screen from above and attack using direct fire patterns. The player must maneuver to avoid incoming shots while firing continuously to destroy enemy aircraft.

Each destroyed enemy awards points, and some enemies release collectible power-ups that grant bonuses such as score increases or weapon upgrades. The player’s aircraft has a health bar; when it is depleted, the plane is destroyed and immediately respawns. The game continues until all available lives are lost, resulting in a game over.

Battle Fire supports a two-player cooperative mode, allowing a second player to join the action at any point during gameplay. Both players share the same scrolling playfield and face enemy formations simultaneously.

466583.overview: The Bard's Lore II: The Dark Tower is a role-playing adventure game that takes players into the mystical world of the Bard's Tale series. The game is set in the city of Lorraine and requires players to assemble a team of adventurers to complete the king's quest. It retains the same playing mechanics as the original Bard's Tale but introduces custom monsters and spells, allowing for a unique gameplay experience. The game was released on December 31, 1998, for DOS and is available for free download. Players must use their cunning and wits to overcome major monsters and prove themselves as worthy adventurers.

466791.overview:
The Battle of Kursk is a strategy game that simulates tank-versus-tank combat on the Eastern Front during World War II. The player selects a side and difficulty level, then engages in a series of one-on-one armored encounters across successive battlefield sections, all in beautiful ASCII.

The battlefield is first shown from an overhead view, where the player controls tank movement across the terrain to gain a favorable position. After moving, the player rotates the turret toward the enemy and switches to a gun-sight view to aim and fire. Combat resolution is calculated using factors such as distance to the target, armor thickness, and the angle of impact. Successful hits may damage or destroy the opposing tank, after which the enemy takes its turn and responds in kind. 

Different difficulty levels affect factors such as armor strength and enemy effectiveness, influencing how engagements unfold as the game progresses.

467398.overview:
Battle Tetris is a Tetris game featuring single-player, two-player, and versus-CPU modes with five difficulty levels. Players arrange tetrominoes into horizontal lines, which vanish to clear space and award points.

Multiplayer is built around a central mechanical piston that separates the two play fields.  This central gauge acts as a tug-of-war meter; when one player clears multiple lines at once, they launch an "attack" that physically pushes this piston toward the opponent. This action forces "garbage" rows—incomplete lines of blocks—up from the bottom of the opponent’s well, rapidly shrinking their available workspace.

467415.overview:
BattleStar is an asteroids-like arcade game centered on multi-directional shooting mechanics viewed from a top-down perspective. The player controls a spacecraft that operates using inertial physics; the craft must be rotated on its axis to change heading, and thrust must be applied to generate momentum for movement. The primary method of interaction is a forward-mounted projectile weapon used to intercept and destroy oncoming targets within a starfield.

The screen functions as a field of combat where the player must manage speed and direction to avoid collisions while tracking multiple enemies. Defensive play involves utilizing the ship's mobility to evade fire or environmental hazards. Success is measured by the accumulation of points through target destruction, while ship integrity or lives are lost upon impact with hostiles or debris. Navigation requires the player to balance the application of thrust with the ship's rotation to maintain control during high-speed exchanges.

467417.overview:
Released the same year as its predecessor, BattleStar 2 works differently from it. What remains unchanged is the movement mechanics inspired by Asteroids: the spaceship can be rotated left and right, and movement can be initiated either forward or backward. Once in motion, the ship is governed by inertia.

To acquire new weapons and additional energy, players must visit planets that occasionally appear in the levels. When a planet is encountered, the view switches the game to a first-person view, where the player controls a reticle to destroy as many approaching spaceships as possible before time runs out.

The objective of each level is to destroy the BattleStar flying through the stage.

467471.overview:
Beaubourg is a puzzle game centered on the industrial architecture of the Centre National d'Art et de Culture Georges-Pompidou in Paris. The narrative follows the management of the building's external technical networks, specifically its iconic color-coded conduit systems. In a conceptual reflection of the actual structure’s "inside-out" design, the player takes on the role of an architect or technician responsible for organizing the flow of resources through the exposed piping that defines the building's exterior.

The game is played on a two-dimensional grid representing a section of the building's facade. The primary objective is to construct continuous paths for red and blue pipes across the screen. These colors correspond to the functional systems of the real-world Beaubourg center, where blue handles climate control and red handles transportation.

The player interacts with the grid by placing or rotating pipe segments. A core mechanical constraint is that pipes of different colors cannot occupy the same tile or cross each other under standard conditions; intersections are only possible through the use of specialized crossover pieces. Success is determined by the player’s ability to navigate the increasingly complex grid while ensuring that both colored networks reach their designated exit points without interruption. The interface utilizes a top-down perspective, displaying the mechanical segments as bold, primary-colored lines against a neutral structural background.

467486.overview:
Beerworm is an arcade snake game following a worm navigating dark, enclosed environments with the primary objective of consuming alcoholic beverages and food.

Movement is continuous, and the worm is directed through a rectangular play area to collect items while avoiding contact with the perimeter or its own body. Navigational challenges are created by static obstacles and the worm's increasing length, which grows with each item consumed.

471191.overview:
Bobenstein 3D is a humorous first-person shooter where players take control of Bob on a mission to track down the culprit behind his ruined cheese and reclaim the coveted Swiss cheese.

To complete the game, Bob must navigate multiple levels, battling enemies along the way. His arsenal consists of five non-lethal weapons that put a non-lethal spin on classic shooter tropes - like a water pistol instead of a standard firearm and rotten eggs in place of grenades. Additionally, players can collect and utilize various items, such as key cards and cookies. The latter restore life energy, which depletes upon taking damage. If Bob runs out of health, the game ends.

471192.overview: Body Slam All-Star Wrestling is an arcade-fighting game developed by Junkyard, released in 1995. The game is available on PC and offers single match or full tournament play for one or two players. It features crisp VGA graphics, smooth animations, and an excellent control scheme, especially for special moves. The game is highly recommended for fans of wrestling games and is considered a quality title from the developer Junkyard, known for their Match Day Manager football simulation.

472324.overview:
ZZT is a 1991 action-adventure puzzle video game and game creation system. Best of ZZT is a kind of sequel that showcases what ZZT can do.

Epic held a Game Design Contest to find the best fanmade games for ZZT.  The entries from this contest were used to create two new game worlds, 'The Secret of Headhunter Isle' and 'Royal Treasures' which Epic released under the name Best of ZZT.

472369.overview:
Biodomes is a side-scrolling shooter set in a future where Earth is uninhabitable due to nuclear warfare. Human civilization has migrated to a distant exoplanet to establish new colonies. These settlements are housed within massive, climate-controlled domes. 

The player controls a spacecraft that moves across a horizontal plane, navigating through cavernous landscapes and industrial environments. The craft maintains a constant forward momentum, requiring the player to maneuver around terrain and architectural barriers while engaging enemies.

472406.overview:
Yet another early conversion of the classic casino game, based on a previous version written for the Compucolor II. The computer deals, using a standard deck, and the player attempts to rack up cash by beating the dealer's hands: the hand closest to a sum of 21 wins; exceed 21 and you bust; if both player and dealer have the same total it's a push, and neither side wins.

As per usual, each side receives one card at a time and decides whether to hit, stand, double down, or split; if the dealer's first card is an ace, the player is offered an insurance bet. The house rules: $500 is the maximum bet, and blackjack pays 1.5 to 1.

472423.overview:
Buffalo Creek Software's Blackjack is based on standard casino rules where the player competes against a dealer. The objective is to achieve a hand value closer to 21 than the dealer without exceeding it.

The game tracks the player's total funds across multiple rounds. Depending on the specific distribution method (often found as shareware or part of BBS software collections), the game operates as a single-player experience where the computer automates all dealer actions and hand resolutions.

472424.overview:
Blackjack is a casino game where the player aims to beat a computer dealer by obtaining a hand total closer to 21 without going over. The action takes place on a green tabletop interface. A status bar at the top displays the player's total bankroll and the current bet amount.

Large graphical cards are dealt to the center of the screen, with the player's current point total listed as a numerical "Count" above their hand. The dealer's cards are positioned to the right, featuring a custom "Mirus Casino" card-back design for face-down cards. The system uses visual representations of a standard 52-card deck, including stylized suits and face cards.

474347.overview:
A bunch of prisoners have escaped from a prison bus and you, as the Sheriff's deputy, must take them out. Unfortunately, they have had help in escaping, and have been supplied with guns. 

Blood Bath at Red Falls is a shooting gallery game where the enemies are digitized actors who pop up from behind cover on the different screens. You can shoot for other items including ammo, a better gun, extra hits and lives. Be careful not to shoot innocent hostages who might get in the way. There are three difficulty levels: Easy, Bring it on, and Bad Ass.

474424.overview: Baron Baldric: A Grave Overture is the shareware version of Baron Baldric: A Grave Adventure. It includes three levels that are not part of the 10-level registered game. Gameplay mechanics and objectives are the same: the Baron must explore the crypts while collecting treasure, food and flint to maintain sources of light, and avoid various traps and perils, including the wolf-ghost of his ancestor Baron Lazarus.

477364.overview:
Bomb Jack is an unofficial platform game based on the 1984 arcade game of the same name. The player takes the role of Jack, a superhero who travels through a series of single-screen stages set against backgrounds inspired by famous landmarks. Each stage is filled with bombs that must be collected while hostile creatures patrol the playfield.

Bomb Jack recreates the gameplay of the original arcade game. Each level is cleared by collecting every bomb on the screen while avoiding enemies that move in distinct patterns. Jack can run, perform high jumps and alter his movement while airborne, allowing him to reach bombs placed both on platforms and in open space. Collecting bombs in the order they light up awards additional points, while bonus items periodically appear to provide score multipliers, extra lives or temporarily turn enemies into collectible bonus items. The game consists of fixed-screen stages that increase in difficulty as enemy speed and behaviour become more challenging.

477368.overview:
Bomb Zone is a science fiction action game in which the player battles waves of hostile killer drones inside a hazardous arena filled with explosive bombs. The objective is to survive each stage by eliminating every drone before advancing to the next.

The game is played from a fixed top-down perspective. Each stage contains several bombs already scattered around the arena, with additional bombs appearing over time. Rather than attacking enemies directly, the player shoots the bombs to trigger explosions that destroy nearby drones. Explosions leave permanent craters that block movement for the player and most enemies, gradually changing the layout of the arena throughout the level.

Bombs also detonate automatically after a delay, with their colour indicating how close they are to exploding. The player has access to a temporary force field that provides protection from enemy collisions and projectiles, although repeated use reduces the score. Enemy projectiles can also be reflected if fired directly at a drone, requiring careful timing and positioning. As the game progresses, new enemy types appear and movement speeds increase, making later stages more difficult.

479957.overview:
Boomerang is a competitive action game centered on a boomerang duel between two opponents. Players face each other in enclosed arenas, optionally filled with maze walls that create obstacles and hiding places. The objective is to outscore the opposing player by landing successful hits with a thrown boomerang before they do.

Matches take place either in open arenas or in one of several pre-generated mazes, with the selected layout remaining in use throughout the game. A point is awarded for each successful hit, and the first player to score ten hits wins the match. Version 2.0 also includes a tournament mode for up to eight participants, automatically organizing a series of head-to-head matches and recording player statistics.

479976.overview:
This super-small version of Tetris is written to fit into the 512-byte boot sector of a floppy disk. Assembly source code is included with the game, along with a program to install it onto any diskette.

The basic elements of Tetris are all here: the falling blocks can be rotated, moved and dropped to complete solid horizontal lines; the filled-up lines are cleared away to make room for more, and to prevent the pile from growing to the top of the playfield. However, the game doesn't keep score, doesn't show you the next piece, and doesn't speed up as you progress - these non-essentials have been dispensed with, making the game small enough to self-boot in half a kilobyte (without taking up any of the disk's visible space at all).

479977.overview:
The sequel to the 1989 game Waterloo takes us back to the village of Borodino on the 7th of September, 1812, during the bloodiest battle of Napoleon's invasion of Russia.

As in the previous game, the player is observing the battle area through a 3D perspective while issuing commands by typing in certain pre-defined text commands that are combined with the names of commanders, places, and the time of execution. Players receive reports from their officers indicating whether or not the orders have been carried out to the letter.

479995.overview:
The first in LonaiSoft's series of Brave Bubble Dragon games, this is pretty much a direct clone of Bubble Bobble: two plucky but affable dragons battle their way through a series of platform-laden screens, disposing of their enemies by blowing bubbles that can trap them, and collecting prodigious amounts of food along the way.

The bubbles may be jumped on, to carry your dragon into otherwise-inaccessible areas, or popped by touching them: if the burst bubble contains a trapped enemy, it'll turn into an edible bonus. In familiar fashion, certain types of bubbles may be used as weapons; power-up items can bestow special abilities; bubbles that spell out 'EXTEND' can be collected for a bonus (one million points, in this case); and even Baron Von Blubba gets his own counterpart.

Unlike Bubble Bobble, however, consecutive stages are grouped into worlds - each with its own theme, complete with a boss creature which must be disposed of using special powers. Other innovations include quirks like teleporting doors and different types of (timed) bonus stages.

480199.overview: British Square is a computer adaptation of the abstract board game of the same name. Two players take turns placing pieces on a 5×5 grid. A piece cannot be placed in a square sharing an edge with an opponent's piece. Play continues until neither player can make another legal move, and the player controlling the most squares wins.

480203.overview: Brix 3: Superlogic is a standalone mission pack for Brix 2 Deluxe with 56 new levels.

480204.overview: Brix 2 is a Breakout variant. The objective is to eliminate all blocks located in the center of the screen by directing a ball toward them. Players control four paddles - positioned on each side of the screen - which must be maneuvered to prevent the ball from exiting the play area, as doing so results in the loss of a life. The left and right paddles move together, as do the top and bottom paddles. Certain blocks trigger effects when struck, such as spawning additional balls or expanding paddle size. Additionally, alien characters move across the playfield; hitting them awards bonus points, and they respawn immediately. The game ends when all player lives are lost.

480206.overview: Brix 4: Genius is a standalone level pack for Brix 2.

480221.overview:
Bubu Chuang Tong Guan is an action game similar to Bomberman. It stars a green octopus traveling through a series of themed worlds filled with hostile creatures and obstacles. Each world consists of multiple stages in which the octopus searches for a hidden key that reveals the route to the exit. Progressing through every stage leads to a boss encounter before advancing to the next world.

Players guide the octopus through maze-like stages, placing small black octopi that function as bombs. Their explosions defeat enemies, destroy breakable rocks, and uncover hidden items. The key required to complete each stage is concealed beneath destructible terrain. After finding it, a skull marker appears elsewhere in the level; destroying it reveals the exit door. The game is divided into themed worlds, each ending with a boss battle.

480222.overview:
Thought frogs had it easy? Bugfeast is here to shatter your idyllic concept of the little green hoppers' daily lives, and show you just how tough it gets in the wild - even when all you wanna do is catch a bunch of flies. Your ASCII amphibian can hop left and right, and extend its tongue to grab the fat juicy insects. But with those huge desert spiders out to get you, and mischievous kids trying to trap you for their amusement, it's a harsh life out there.

Being a frog, you can try to hide underwater... but that will only attract the fiendish water-snakes. With some luck you'll be able to squish the spiders and avoid the cage traps, and with even more luck, you may awaken the cactus-dweller to increase your scoring. The "supertongue" gives you greater range, but uses more of your limited number of licks; if you run out, it'll kill you as surely as any vermin. And if this all sounds too tough, the difficulty level is adjustable.

480223.overview: Buick Dimensions is a piece of automotive advertisement software that contains within it a nine hole golfing game based on the Buick Classic at the Westchester Country Club.

480244.overview:
Builder is a game of environmental anxiety. The world is closing in on you, and you need to escape. To do this, you observe your environment, build footholds, and destroy obstacles to your progress.

There are at least three ways to play Builder. At first you have a puzzle platformer � obtuse, and full of glitches. Often the puzzles have more than one solution; the way that you choose depends on your perspective, and may affect what comes next. When you�ve learned your way around, the game becomes a race. And when you embrace all that is wrong with the world � well. You may be on the right track.

Builder is designed on the 20-year-old Game-Maker engine by Recreational Software Designs.

480262.overview: Originally made for mainframes, Bullseye is a simple text-based simulation of the perennial pub game of Darts, for up to 20(!) players. The target board is divided into zones of 10, 20, 30 and 40 points, and each player in turn selects a move: fast overarm, controlled overarm, or underarm - the type of throw dictates the probable outcome. Once all throws have been scored, a new round begins, until one or more players win by reaching 200 points.

480265.overview:
Bulsajo Duck is a Korean shmupset in a futuristic world where Earth has been invaded by an alien race known as the Duck tribe. A faction of the invaders joins forces with humanity to establish the Earth Defense Force. Players take the role of a duck soldier fighting against the hostile alien forces in an effort to repel the invasion.

The game uses one-hit deaths, making precise movement and positioning essential. Defeated enemies leave behind power-ups that improve the player's weapons, increasing offensive capabilities as the game progresses. Each stage culminates in a large boss battle that must be overcome before advancing to the next area.

482730.overview: Guide a smiling face through a maze to the exit in the bottom-right corner. The passages are initially hidden and become visible as you explore, follow junctions and retrace dead ends. Miroslav Němeček's maze game was designed for preschool children.

482735.overview: A small arcade shooting game made to promote Boovie. It uses Boovie's graphics engine and characters, replacing that game's puzzles with shooting and quick reactions. Shoot targets and try to earn a high score.
